_provenance.purpose: WS2 T3.2 Step 2 - compositional cardinal-number generation data, shared by faTextNormalize.ts and fa/text.rs
_provenance.status: landed Step 2 (data only) - not yet consumed by either implementation
notes: cardinals0to99 extends the existing GERMAN_CARDINALS_0_30 table verbatim for 0-30, then continues the fully regular {unit-combining-form}und{tens} pattern to 99 - German has NO space wall anywhere in 0-99 (nor in hundreds/thousands, see below), unlike the other four languages.
Combining form of 'eins' is 'ein' (matches the existing table's own 'einundzwanzig' spelling) - every other unit is unchanged in combining position.

German cardinals fully concatenate (no space, no hyphen) through the hundreds and thousands ranges: 'einhundertdreiundzwanzig' (123) is one word. THIS DOES NOT EXTEND TO MILLION+: 'Million'/'Millionen' are real German nouns and take a space ('eine Million', 'zwei Millionen') - correcting this session's own earlier over-broad claim that German has no wall at any magnitude (see t32-step2-precheck-multiword-wall.md) - the wall exists for de too, just starting three orders of magnitude later than the other four languages.

'ß' is not in the German FA vocab (spike G1) - values below are the pre-substitution vocab-safe spelling ('dreissig' not 'dreißig'), matching the existing table's own convention; applyLanguageSpecificSubstitutions still runs on the final composed string regardless.

hundred.note: countWordOverride 'ein' (STEP 3b-iii fix, generator implementation): dropsOneMultiplier is false (count=1 IS shown, per 'einhundert'), but cardinals0to99['1'] is the bare-citation form 'eins', not the combining form 'ein' this position needs (same eins->ein rule cardinals0to99's own 21/31/.../91 entries already bake in internally) - without this override the generator would compose 'einshundert', not 'einhundert'. Mirrors the pattern million's own countWordOverride ('eine') already established for the same count=1/dropsOneMultiplier=false combination.

scale.note: countWordOverride 'ein', same reason and precedent as hundred's own note above - without it the generator would compose 'einstausend', not 'eintausend' (and the yearReading 'compound' candidate's own documented example, 'eintausendneunhundertachtundneunzig', would come out wrong).
Million is a capitalized noun taking feminine 'eine' (not the generic 'ein' combining form) for count=1 - grammatical gender agreement, not a typo.

yearReading.rationale: The matcher is not language-gated - it applies the same n % 100 >= threshold rule to every language's digit tokens regardless of content language (confirmed in t32-step3b-i-year-reading-measurement.md). This mirrors that structure only, not a German-specific reading convention verified against a real corpus - revisitable when a real de corpus exists.
yearReading.matcherParityNote: The x00–x09 cardinal fallback (n % 100 < threshold, e.g. 1900-1909, 2000-2009) is a known matcher defect being deliberately mirrored here, not independently corrected - if the matcher's threshold or behavior is ever corrected, this policy must be updated in the same change. The two sides must not be fixed independently.
yearReading.note: DETERMINED (operator ruling, Step 3b-ii): selectionPolicy now encodes the same conditional-rule shape as en's (n % 100 >= threshold -> 'hundertgruppe', else -> 'compound'). Both candidates fuse into a single concatenated word regardless of which is picked (no representability difference, unlike en/es/fr/pt) - 'hundertgruppe' = hundred-grouped colloquial year reading ('neunzehnhundertachtundneunzig'), 'compound' = literal arithmetic decomposition ('eintausendneunhundertachtundneunzig'). Still consumed by nothing - Step 3b-iii wires this into faTextNormalize.ts/fa/text.rs.
